blocks.text: NEW TESTAMENT
Judas Barsabas. Chosen at Jerusalem with Silas to carry the apostles’ letter to Antioch, where he exhorted and confirmed the brethren.
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“Being prophets also themselves” (Acts 15:32): one of the “chief men among the brethren” (Acts 15:22)
ERA
New Testament AD 1–60
IN THE DAYS OF
No ruler named beside him
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Acts 15 · Chosen and sent
THE CALL
How the word first came
ACTS 15 · CHOSEN AND SENT
“Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:”
Acts 15:22 (KJV) →
HOW THE WORD KEPT COMING
The letter he carried said the two “shall also tell you the same things by mouth.” Acts 15:27
From the textActs calls Judas and Silas prophets and says what they did, not what they said: they “exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.” Acts 15:32
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
The letter from Jerusalem
“For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;”
Acts 15:28 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO THE BRETHREN AT ANTIOCH
“exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.”
Acts 15:32 (KJV) →
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Silas
Paul
Barnabas
Joseph called Barsabas
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“After they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.” Acts names him no more. Acts 15:33

Scholars' viewThe KJV goes on, “Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still” (Acts 15:34). Barnes notes that this verse “is missing in many mss.”, and Lumby suggests it began as a note to explain Acts 15:40. Acts 15:34 Acts 15:40 [76][77]
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Probably his brother
Matthew Poole (1683–1685); E. H. Plumptre (Ellicott’s commentary); Grotius and Wolf (as reported by Meyer)

Lumby calls Barsabas a patronymic, a name from the father; Plumptre: “It is a natural inference that the two were brothers”, and so that Judas had been among the Lord’s followers. Poole states it outright. Acts 1:23 Acts 15:22 [70][69][71][73]
It cannot be shown
Jamieson, Fausset and Brown (1871); H. A. W. Meyer; J. R. Lumby (Cambridge Bible, 1885), who calls it a conjecture
Jamieson, Fausset and Brown: “nor can it be shown that he was a brother of ‘Joseph called Barsabas’”; “nothing is known of him beyond what is here said.” Acts 15:22 [72][71][73]
Perhaps the same man
Albert Barnes, as a possibility; H. Ewald (as reported by Knowling, 1900)
Barnes: “Possibly the same who was nominated to the vacant place in the apostleship”; Knowling reports that Ewald “thinks that he was actually identical with him”. Acts 1:23 Acts 15:22 [74][75]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 2
Acts 1 Acts 15
PASSAGES · 2
Acts 1:23 Acts 15:22–35
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Acts records none of his words.
Scripture does not say what became of him after he returned from Antioch.
